claim: Muir Woods is ~30 min by car, Sausalito ~20 min, Half Moon Bay ~40 min, all easy day trips with redwoods, houseboats and coastal cliffs respectively.
quote: Muir Woods is close to downtown at around a 30-minute drive... Sausalito is a 20-minute drive away... Half Moon Bay is just a 40-minute drive from the city and is a lovely surf haven.

claim: Napa Valley stretches ~30 miles with over 400 wineries; Point Reyes National Seashore offers beaches, wildlife and hiking close to the city.
quote: this lush valley stretches approximately 30 miles and is home to over 400 wineries... Point Reyes National Seashore is a coastal paradise offering a stunning blend of beaches, wildlife, and hiking trails.

claim: Muir Woods requires parking or shuttle reservations seven days a week year-round; weekend shuttle from Larkspur/Sausalito is $4 round-trip, kids 15 and under free.
quote: Reservations for parking... and seats on the Muir Woods shuttle are now required seven days a week, year-round... shuttle tickets costing $4.00 per adult (round-trip), and children 15 and younger riding free.

claim: A scenic ~30-minute ferry from San Francisco (Pier 41) reaches Sausalito with views of the Golden Gate, Bay Bridge and Alcatraz; ferries also connect to the Muir Woods shuttle.
quote: A scenic 30-minute ferry ride takes you from San Francisco to Sausalito... look out for the Bay Bridge, the Golden Gate Bridge, and Alcatraz Island.

claim: 2026 Muni adult single ride is $2.85 with Clipper/MuniMobile ($3.00 cash), cable car $9, Visitor Passports $15/1-day, $35/3-day, $47/7-day.
quote: Clipper/MuniMobile: $2.85... Cash: $3.00... Cable Car Single Ride: $9.00... 1-Day: $15.00... 3-Day: $35.00... 7-Day: $47.00

claim: Muni caps standard daily fares at $5.70 (further rides free that day); cable car single rides are $9; SFO-to-downtown BART is $11.15 one way; tap-to-pay contactless launched late 2025 so no physical Clipper needed.
quote: Muni caps standard daily fares at $5.70. Once you hit that amount, the rest of your rides that day are free... A round-trip fare from SFO to downtown San Francisco is $22.30 ($11.15 one-way).

claim: SFMTA is considering 2026 changes replacing the $5.70 day pass with Clipper fare-capping (free after two paid trips) and raising cable car fares, with cash excluded from capping.
quote: it would be replaced with "fare capping": After paying for two trips in one day with a Clipper card, credit card or other digital account, additional rides for the rest of the day would be free. However, fare capping wouldn't apply to cash fares.

claim: Fall (Sept-Oct) and April are the best, clearest, warmest times to visit (highs ~70-75F); May-August is the foggy season with August ('Fogust') the peak.
quote: Fall is widely considered the best season to visit San Francisco... September, October, and April typically have the least fog... the foggy months in San Francisco are May, June, July and most of August. August, aptly known as "Fogust".

claim: San Francisco has sharp microclimates: the western edge (Golden Gate Park, Sunset, Richmond) is coolest and foggiest while the Mission District and Fisherman's Wharf can be sunny simultaneously, with hills like Twin Peaks blocking fog.
quote: The western edge of the city is the coolest and foggiest. Golden Gate Park, the Sunset District and the Richmond District are known for their fog. For sunnier options... head to the Mission District.

claim: Nob Hill and Union Square are the safest, most central bases for visitors; Fisherman's Wharf, Chinatown and North Beach are also good first-timer areas.
quote: Nob Hill and Union Square are easily the two safest places to stay in San Francisco due to low crime rates... Fisherman's Wharf, Union Square, Chinatown and Nob Hill are good areas for first time visitors.

claim: The Tenderloin (west of Union Square) should be avoided day and night due to open drug use and unsanitary conditions, as should isolated Bayview-Hunters Point.
quote: The Tenderloin is located just west of Union Square... It is the epicenter of the homeless and drug crisis... this area should be avoided at all costs and is impassable at night.

claim: Car break-ins are the single most common crime affecting tourists in San Francisco, with rental cars targeted and windows smashed in minutes even in daylight at tourist stops.
quote: Car break-ins are the single most common crime affecting tourists in San Francisco. Thieves target rental cars in particular, and a smashed window can happen in minutes — even in broad daylight at popular tourist stops.
